messages:
maya: FYI noticed p50 on /v1/generate dropped ~30ms right after we flipped the new routing-policy. p99 looks unchanged but p95 crept up a bit.
linus: hmm, did we change any sampling or aggregation configs with that rollout? @sarah any console merge-mode changes?
sarah: we switched the rollup merge to 'weight' for that route yesterday to respect canary weights — could bias small quantiles.
ana: oops small typo: it's ana (but also, we did flip sample_origin tagging for the canary client to 'sdk-v2')
ana: deploy-bot said: "deploy complete: routing-policy/v3 -> canary=20%"
linus: can you paste the PromQL or tdigest query you used to spot this, maya?
maya: sure — quick check I ran in console:
```
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum(rate(latency_bucket{endpoint="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, sample_origin))
```
maya: when I group by sample_origin I see p50 for "sdk-v2" is ~40ms lower than "sdk-v1"; overall p50 decreased because sdk-v2 has a lot of cached/prefix hits.
sarah: that matches the rollout. sdk-v2 traffic is hitting KV cache more aggressively (shorter seqs + prefix cache), so bulk of requests look faster.
ana: but p95 increased — my suspicion is that a small subset of requests routed to a different variant (no-cache path) are longer and are now more visible at p95.
linus: so UI-level merge mode 'weight' is producing an overall p50 that doesn't reflect the tail experience of non-cached users.
sarah: right. console currently shows a single percentile line per endpoint. we should expose a split by tags (cache_hit, sample_origin) or annotate when merge-mode=weight is used.
maya: +1. If product teams see p50 improve they might think rollout is safe while a non-trivial cohort still has higher p95/p99.
linus: proposal: add a small "Percentiles by tag" quick toggle (group by cache_hit / sample_origin) and a tooltip explaining merge behaviors and sample_rate effects.
sarah: API debate: do we compute per-tag percentiles server-side (costly) or compute on-the-fly in console from rollup histograms? both have tradeoffs.
ana: I think we can compute from stored tdigest rollups for the selected tags; cost should be bounded if we limit to top-3 tags in UI. otherwise fallback to server precompute for long windows.
maya: for the short-term: can we surface a banner on the dashboard when route merge-mode!=uniform and sample_rate<1? something like: "Percentiles reflect a merged view weighted by route traffic — enable per-tag breakdown to inspect cohorts." 
linus: I'll spin up a synthetic test to reproduce: replay 1k requests with sdk-v1 vs sdk-v2 weights and confirm p50/p95 behavior. assign to me.
sarah: thanks. also filing a console bug/feature: tag #rollout-ui and assign to @eng-console. include queries and the canary weight timeline.
maya: filed: 4387654321-ui-rollout-percentile-annotation (link attached in ticket)
ana: quick note: if sample_rate differs across SDKs we should treat that as a critical annotation; it invalidates direct percentile comparisons.
linus: running audit now, will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: monitor: routing-policy/v3 canary=20% at 2026-03-20T15:22:09Z"
